title: Home for supper
notes: Your family keeps its own hours now. Around seven the whole household sits down to supper at the long table — Father at the head, Mother at the foot.
After supper Father takes his chair by the fire, Mother her spinning wheel, Grandfather the hearth, and the twins the window seat. By nine everyone is in bed.
New rooms at the Homestead: Father and Mother's bedchamber off the hall, with a great curtained box bed; and Grandfather's room upstairs, with a spare bed for guests.

After the wedding Princess Madison lives at the Homestead: baking with your mother, writing to her father at your desk, reading to the twins — then supper, the stars from your balcony, and your bed, which is hers now too.
One night in three a friend stays over: Squire Matthew, and Sir Joshua once the realm is at peace.

The barn can be walked into now: three stalls (the old mule is a mule again), a hayloft, and the Stables at the stalls. Hal the farmhand works there by day, sits by his lantern of an evening, and sleeps up in the loft.
A basket by the hall fire for your companion.
Wake anyone in bed and they'll mumble something sleepy, then drift off again.

title: Lights out
notes: Shops and inns now have a small bedroom at the back. After dark the shopkeeper is tucked up in bed — wake them and they'll grumble, then sell to you anyway.
In the evening the innkeeper comes round from the bar and sits by the fire; from about half past eight everyone who lives there is in bed until morning.
Families at home sit at the table or stand by the hearth in the evening, then sleep in their own beds.
A door behind the throne now leads to the Royal Chambers: a bedchamber for King Karl and one for Princess Madison, with a guard at the door. At night you'll find them asleep there.
By day Princess Madison stands beside the throne in the great hall (until she's taken, and again once she's home).
People in dungeons stay where they are.

title: Word spreads
notes: Townsfolk now answer to what you've done: afraid while their own chapel is bound, overjoyed when you've just cleansed it, grateful and at ease after.
Word spreads: villages you haven't reached yet pass on news of the towns you've freed — and wonder if it was you.
Help someone in a village and the whole village hears of it.
Visit at night and the family welcomes you in from the dark.
Guards, the night watch and the children each have their own way of saying it — and once the Demon King is beaten, the whole realm is at peace.
Old warnings about demons on the road fall silent once a village is free.

title: Home at night
notes: At dusk the villagers walk home along the lanes and go in at their own doors (the children first); at dawn they come out and walk back to their day.
Visit them at night: knock on a door and you'll find the family in, by the fire or at the table.
The town guards change the watch at dusk and dawn: the day guard walks off to the barracks and a night guard with a lantern takes the post.
Village homes are now real houses: a hall with the hearth, table and chairs, a partition with a doorway, and a bedchamber with a bed for everyone who lives there, a chest at each bed's foot.

title: The villagers, dressed and at ease
notes: Each village now dresses in its own cloth: Hearthvale's warm browns and greens, Saltmere's whites and sea blues, Dusthaven's sand and indigo, Crystalpeak's bright weaves, and so on — no two neighbours quite alike.
Town guards wear their town's steel and colours.
More hairstyles and hair colours, bearded men, and grey-haired elders who stoop a little.

Standing about, townsfolk settle into a stance of their own — hands behind the back, arms crossed or folded, hands clasped, thumbs in the belt — and breathe and look around; guards stand square at their posts.

title: Hats, hoods and crowns
notes: King Karl has his hair again, drawn back into a bun, and wears a proper crown: a gilt band set with stones, eight pearl-tipped points and a cross over red velvet.
Hats and hoods across the realm now sit on people's heads, not at their mouths or necks; hoods cover the head with no hair poking through.
The minstrels' harp is held lower so you can see the harpist, and the recorder player holds the recorder below her chin.

title: The throne hall rebuilt
notes: King Karl's throne hall is rebuilt in warm Romanesque stone: round arches on thick pillars, an open oak roof, amber glass, torches and iron wheels of candles.
The king's minstrels play old hymns beside the throne: harp, hurdy-gurdy, lute, recorder and frame drum.
King Karl now truly sits on his throne — a carved oak throne with velvet padding, gilt lions' heads and a footstool.
The Royal Guards' helms now sit properly over their heads.
The guards stand at their posts and look about the hall; the king shifts and looks around from his throne; the minstrels play their instruments in time with the music.
Each village's banner is now its own battle-worn shield on the pillars, in the village's colour with the crest of the realm in gold and its sign embroidered round the edge.
A shield stays under a dark cloth until you cleanse that village's chapel; the next time you enter the hall, the cloth falls away.

title: The launcher
notes: Kingdom's Last Knight now has a launcher for Windows, Mac and Linux: play offline, update when you choose.
Back up, restore and export your saves. A backup is made before every update.
Installed on a Chromebook, the game keeps your version until you tap Update.

title: The beasts' heads
notes: Every pelt's head is reshaped: bear, wolf, fox, lion, stag, ram and raven, with jaws, noses, eyes, ears, antlers and horns.
With the hood down, the head rests on top of a shield slung on your back.

title: Pelts that move as one
notes: Pelts and hoods are one soft piece that moves with your shoulders: no more coming apart when you run.
Animal hoods wear a short cape hung diagonally from the left shoulder.
With the hood down, the beast's head hangs behind your neck.

title: A sturdier shield
notes: The shield stays on your forearm in every pose, keeps its full shape on your back and faces square when you block.
You can walk while blocking.

title: Boots and greaves
notes: Thicker boots and shoes; trousers tuck in under greaves.
Capes and cloaks lie under a shield on your back.

title: Legs & boots
notes: One Legs & boots choice: each set brings its own, plus common kits — trousers and boots, barefoot, armoured legs with steel or leather boots.

title: Gloves
notes: Gloves come with your vambraces and bend with your fingers: plated, leather, fur-cuffed, decorative, fingerless and wraps.

title: Armour that stays put
notes: Armour no longer loads messy or comes loose when you move or attack.
